title: Arduino Basics: Digital Input & Output
learning_objective: Students can write and explain an Arduino program that reads a digital input (a button) and controls a digital output (an LED) based on that input.

sections.title: What is a microcontroller?
sections.content: An Arduino is a small computer that runs one program in a loop, reading inputs and controlling outputs in real time. Unlike a laptop, it has no operating system to switch between — it just runs your code, forever, from the moment it powers on.

sections.title: Digital output: blinking an LED
sections.content: digitalWrite(pin, HIGH) sends 5V to a pin; digitalWrite(pin, LOW) sends 0V. Wiring an LED with a current-limiting resistor to a digital pin lets code turn it on and off. The classic first program (Blink) toggles a pin HIGH and LOW with delay() calls in loop().

sections.title: Digital input: reading a button
sections.content: pinMode(pin, INPUT_PULLUP) configures a pin to read a button press, using the Arduino's internal pull-up resistor so the pin reads HIGH when unpressed and LOW when pressed. digitalRead(pin) returns the current state.

sections.title: Combining input and output: button-controlled LED
sections.content: Reading the button state each loop() iteration and using an if statement to set the LED pin HIGH or LOW accordingly is the first program that connects input to output — the foundation for every more complex Arduino project.
